proposal.title: Mechanism-diversified self-masking augmentation with group-robust boosting for missingness shift (unvalidated hypothesis)
proposal.hypothesis: Native-NaN HistGradientBoosting (HGB) trained under MCAR20% learns split directions for missing values tied to one mechanism. Its errors under own-value MNAR come from that learned mask-to-label association, not from lost information. We propose training on extra masks applied to already-observed entries. Some of these masks depend on the entry's own observed value, high or low. A group-DRO reweighting across mask mechanisms then penalizes reliance on any single mask-to-label association. Prediction: this lowers the worst-case mAP drop on own-value and reversed MNAR relative to random-mask augmentation. Clean and MCAR mAP should stay within 0.005 of baseline. No universal claim is made.
proposal.mechanism: Random masking alone leaves a mask independent of value. Self-masking applied to observed values creates training regimes where the mask carries value information in both directions. Group DRO then forces the learned missing-branch split directions to work under both. This is a direct intervention on the mask-to-prediction causal edge, not imputation preprocessing.

proposed_primitives.definition: For an observed non-anchor entry x_j, drop it with probability sigmoid(s*a*(q_j(x_j)-0.5)). Here q_j is the empirical CDF of observed training values, s is +1 or -1, and a is fixed at 4. Only observed values are used. Hidden clean values are never used.

Outer loop over HGB refits, 3 rounds. Each round upweights mechanism groups by exp(eta*group log-loss), computed on a mechanism-augmented copy of the validation features. These group weights are passed through sample_weight. No feature scaling is applied, so the weights cannot cancel.

relations.counterfactual_prediction: If the simulator is removed and only random masks remain, the MNAR mAP gain over random-mask augmentation disappears to within seed noise.

relations.type: balances (prevents the dominant augmented group from setting the missing-branch direction)
relations.counterfactual_prediction: If uniform weights are used, the worst-case MNAR mAP is lower, but the mean over mechanisms is roughly unchanged.
MAR and MCAR validation gains should be about zero. If not, the gain is regularization, not mechanism robustness.

assumptions: Narrow assumption: held-out MNAR is per-feature monotone self-masking in its own value, with P(Y|X) stable.
Training-observed value quantiles approximate target quantiles.
Within the augmented family, the anchors' own-value missingness stays at zero.

Failure modes: grouped structural missingness that depends on the label or on latent groups; non-monotone MNAR; and shifts in P(Y|X). All are outside the assumption and are reported as failures, not tuned away.
No unlabeled target-batch statistics are used. Any variant that uses them is declared separately.
strongest_prior_art: arxiv:2507.08280 (MIRRAMS): overlaps in seeking robustness to unseen missingness shift without assuming a mechanism. It differs in using an MI-based neural objective rather than simulated mechanism groups. It is the main comparator, implemented as a small CPU MLP.
arxiv:2512.19602: overlaps in using missingness as augmentation. It differs in that its masks are random, not value-dependent.
arxiv:2603.00046: overlaps in group DRO over availability groups. It differs in grouping by modality combination rather than missingness mechanism.
algorithm: 1. Split the data 60/20/20 and apply the training mask (MCAR20%). Labels are used only for train and validation.
2. Build augmented training copies from the observed entries: G0 = original, G1 = random extra 20%, G2 = self-mask s=+1, G3 = self-mask s=-1.
3. Build the same groups on validation features. MAR and MCAR validation remain untouched for model selection.
4. Fit native-NaN HGB with uniform group weights.
5. For each round r = 1..3: compute group log-loss L_g on the validation groups; set w_g proportional to exp(eta*L_g); refit with sample_weight = w_g.
6. Select eta from {0.5, 1, 2} by mean validation AP over clean, MCAR20, MCAR40, and MAR. Held-out mechanisms are not consulted.
7. Predict at test time from observed values and NaNs only.
8. Report AP, Brier score, and clean AP per mechanism; report worst-case AP; report mean ± std over 10 seeds.
proposal.baseline: B1: native-NaN HGB. B2: HGB with random-mask augmentation matched in augmented row count. B3: MIRRAMS-style MLP.
ablations: A1: drop G2 and G3, matched in row count (edge removal).
A2: uniform weights (removes the DRO edge).
A4: mask-blind control, i.e. HGB on mean-filled values without NaN branching.
A5: shuffle which value the self-mask uses (permuted q_j). This tests that the effect comes from value dependence.
proposal.metric: Primary: mean AP across the three held-out mechanisms, plus worst-case AP. Secondary: Brier score and clean AP.
proposal.falsification: The hypothesis is rejected under any of three outcomes. First, the full method fails to beat A1 by at least 0.01 mean MNAR AP with a paired seed sign test (p<0.05). Second, A5 matches the full method. Third, clean AP drops by more than 0.005.
proposal.feasibility: 5000×20 with 4× augmentation and 4 HGB fits takes about 30 s per seed on a CPU. The MLP comparator takes about 90 s. Both are under 5 minutes.

validation_note: Revalidated saved response: proposed primitive names need not have a specific prefix; known arXiv aliases normalized; grounded edge endpoints included in component list. No semantic content or model calls added.
